package_info.package_versions: Malicious version found on compromised mirror (exact version not specified)
package_info.why_malicious: The distributed HandBrake app was trojanized to include a new variant of the Proton malware, which provides remote access and credential theft capabilities. The legitimate application was replaced on a compromised download server, leading users to unknowingly install malware.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (on application launch or background execution)
execution_context.file_location: Injected into the HandBrake app bundle (likely in main executable or supporting binary)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Proton malware variant (exact code not shown in report, but known behaviors include keylogging, credential theft, and remote command execution)
malicious_snippets.code_language: objective-c (macOS binary, possibly with shell script components)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code establishes persistence, collects user credentials (including keychain data), and exfiltrates this information to a remote command and control server, enabling full remote access and data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code performs credential theft, persistence, and remote access, which are not behaviors expected from a legitimate video transcoder application.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A normal HandBrake app should only perform video transcoding and related file operations, not access sensitive credentials or establish remote connections.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote access and credential collection may be legitimate in enterprise management tools, but never in consumer video transcoding software.

attack_chain.action: User downloads and installs the trojanized HandBrake app from the compromised mirror.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious code bundled with the app

attack_chain.action: On launch, the Proton malware variant executes, establishing persistence and collecting sensitive data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of credentials and remote access

attack_chain.action: Collected credentials and system information are sent to the attacker's command and control server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains remote access and control over the victim's system

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected network connections from a video transcoder app
Access to macOS keychain or credential stores by non-security software
Persistence mechanisms established by non-updater components
file_indicators: HandBrake app bundle with modified or unsigned binaries
Presence of Proton malware components (e.g., launch agents, hidden binaries)
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known Proton C2 infrastructure
Unusual HTTPS POST requests from HandBrake process
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for video transcoder applications (like HandBrake) making network connections, accessing the keychain, or establishing persistence. Check app signatures and hashes against known-good versions. Look for the presence of known Proton malware files or launch agents. Alert on any credential exfiltration attempts or remote command and control activity originating from non-administrative tools.
